title: Ala. Code § 8-19-5 — Unlawful trade practices
content:
Ala. Code § 8-19-5

The following are unlawful trade practices:

(1) Causing confusion or misunderstanding as to the source, sponsorship, approval, or certification of goods or services.

(2) Causing confusion or misunderstanding as to affiliation, connection, or association with, or certification by, another.

(5) Representing that goods or services have sponsorship, approval, characteristics, ingredients, uses, benefits, or quantities that they do not have.

(27) Engaging in any other unconscionable, false, misleading, or deceptive act or practice in the conduct of trade or commerce.

sections.content: Alabama prohibits listed deceptive and unconscionable trade practices in the conduct of trade or commerce.

title: Ala. Code § 35-9A-421 — Landlord remedies; noncompliance

hierarchyPath.label: Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act

content:
Ala. Code § 35-9A-421

sections.content: A landlord may terminate for material tenant noncompliance after written notice allowing at least 14 days to remedy.

title: Ala. Code § 6-5-430 — Personal jurisdiction; long-arm
content:
Ala. Code § 6-5-430

A court of this state may exercise personal jurisdiction over a person or corporation as to a cause of action arising from any of the following acts:

(1) Transacting any business in this state.

(2) Contracting to supply services or things in this state.

(3) Causing tortious injury or damage by an act or omission in this state.

(4) Causing tortious injury or damage in this state by an act or omission outside this state if the person regularly does or solicits business, or engages in any other persistent course of conduct, or derives substantial revenue from goods used or consumed or services rendered in this state.

sections.content: Alabama long-arm statute authorizes personal jurisdiction for listed contacts including transacting business and causing tortious injury in the state.

title: Utah Code § 13-11-4 — Consumer protection
content:
Utah Code § 13-11-4

(1) A deceptive act or practice by a supplier in connection with a consumer transaction violates this chapter whether it occurs before, during, or after the transaction.

(2) Without limiting the scope of Subsection (1), a supplier commits a deceptive act or practice if the supplier knowingly or intentionally:

(a) indicates that the subject of a consumer transaction has sponsorship, approval, performance characteristics, accessories, uses, or benefits, if it has not;

sections.content: Utah prohibits unfair or deceptive trade practices in commerce.

title: Utah Code § 57-22-4 — Landlord-tenant / property
content:
Utah Code § 57-22-4

(1) A renter of a residential rental unit may bring an action in district court or justice court to enforce the renter's rights under this chapter.

(2) A renter may not bring an action under this chapter if the renter is in default in the payment of rent unless the default is based on a good faith claim that the residential rental unit is uninhabitable.

sections.content: Utah residential landlord-tenant termination or possession provision.

title: Vt. Stat. Ann. tit. 9, § 2453 — Consumer protection
content:
Vt. Stat. Ann. tit. 9, § 2453

(a) Unfair methods of competition in commerce and unfair or deceptive acts or practices in commerce are hereby declared unlawful.

(b) It is the intent of the Legislature that in construing subsection (a) of this section, the courts of this State will be guided by the construction of similar terms contained in Section 5(a)(1) of the Federal Trade Commission Act.

sections.content: Vermont prohibits unfair or deceptive trade practices in commerce.

title: Vt. Stat. Ann. tit. 9, § 4467 — Landlord-tenant / property
content:
Vt. Stat. Ann. tit. 9, § 4467

(a) If there is a material noncompliance by the tenant with the rental agreement or a noncompliance with section 4456 of this title materially affecting health and safety, the landlord may deliver a written notice to the tenant specifying the acts and omissions constituting the breach and that the rental agreement will terminate upon a date not less than 30 days after receipt of the notice if the breach is not remedied.

sections.content: Vermont residential landlord-tenant termination or possession provision.

title: W. Va. Code § 46A-6-104 — Consumer protection
content:
W. Va. Code § 46A-6-104

Unfair methods of competition and unfair or deceptive acts or practices in the conduct of any trade or commerce are hereby declared unlawful.

sections.content: West Virginia prohibits unfair or deceptive trade practices in commerce.

title: W. Va. Code § 37-6-6 — Landlord-tenant / property
content:
W. Va. Code § 37-6-6

A tenancy from year to year may be terminated by either party giving notice in writing to the other, of his intention to terminate the same, three months prior to the end of any year; and a tenancy from month to month may be terminated by like notice of one month.

sections.content: West Virginia residential landlord-tenant termination or possession provision.

title: W. Va. Code § 56-3-33 — Personal jurisdiction
content:
W. Va. Code § 56-3-33

(a) The engaging by a nonresident, or by his or her duly authorized agent, in any one or more of the acts specified in subsections (a)(1) through (a)(7) of this section shall be deemed equivalent to an appointment by such nonresident of the Secretary of State, or his or her successor in office, to be his or her true and lawful attorney upon whom may be served all lawful process in any action or proceeding against him or her, in any circuit court in this state, for a cause of action arising out of such acts.

sections.content: West Virginia long-arm / personal jurisdiction statute.

title: Wyo. Stat. Ann. § 40-12-105 — Consumer protection
content:
Wyo. Stat. Ann. § 40-12-105

(a) A person engages in a deceptive trade practice when, in the course of his business and in connection with a consumer transaction, he knowingly:

(i) Represents that merchandise has a source, origin, sponsorship, approval, accessories or uses it does not have;

(xv) Engages in unfair or deceptive acts or practices.

sections.content: Wyoming prohibits unfair or deceptive trade practices in commerce.

title: Wyo. Stat. Ann. § 1-21-1003 — Landlord-tenant / property
content:
Wyo. Stat. Ann. § 1-21-1003

(a) A person entitled to possession of premises which are unlawfully held by another may bring a civil action for possession.

sections.content: Wyoming residential landlord-tenant termination or possession provision.

title: Wyo. Stat. Ann. § 5-1-107 — Personal jurisdiction
content:
Wyo. Stat. Ann. § 5-1-107

(a) A Wyoming court may exercise jurisdiction on any basis not inconsistent with the Wyoming or United States constitution.

sections.content: Wyoming long-arm / personal jurisdiction statute.

title: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.1 — Notice to terminate tenancy
content:
Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.1

(a) Notwithstanding Section 1946, a hiring of residential real property for a term not specified by the parties is deemed to be renewed as stated in this section.

(b) An owner of a residential dwelling giving notice pursuant to this section shall give notice at least 60 days prior to the proposed date of termination if the tenant has resided in the dwelling for at least one year.

sections.content: California requires at least 60 days' notice to terminate a residential tenancy of one year or more.

title: Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.150 — CCPA private right of action for data breach
content:
Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.150

(a)(1) Any consumer whose nonencrypted and nonredacted personal information, as defined in subparagraph (A) of paragraph (1) of subdivision (d) of Section 1798.81.5, is subject to an unauthorized access and exfiltration, theft, or disclosure as a result of the business's violation of the duty to implement and maintain reasonable security procedures and practices appropriate to the nature of the information to protect the personal information may institute a civil action.

sections.content: CCPA authorizes a private civil action for certain data breaches resulting from unreasonable security practices.

title: N.Y. Gen. Bus. Law § 349 — Deceptive acts and practices
content:
N.Y. Gen. Bus. Law § 349

(a) Deceptive acts or practices in the conduct of any business, trade or commerce or in the furnishing of any service in this state are hereby declared unlawful.

(h) In addition to the right of action granted to the attorney general pursuant to this section, any person who has been injured by reason of any violation of this section may bring an action in his own name to enjoin such unlawful act or practice, an action to recover his actual damages or fifty dollars, whichever is greater, or both such actions.

sections.content: New York prohibits deceptive acts or practices in business and provides a private right of action.

title: N.Y. Real Prop. Law § 232-a — Notice to terminate monthly tenancy
content:
N.Y. Real Prop. Law § 232-a

No monthly tenant or tenant from month to month shall be removed from any lands or buildings in the city of New York on the grounds of holding over his term unless at least thirty days before the expiration of the term the landlord or his agent serve upon the tenant a notice in writing to the effect that the landlord elects to terminate the tenancy.

sections.content: In NYC, month-to-month tenancies require at least thirty days' written termination notice before holdover removal.

title: Tex. Bus. & Com. Code § 17.46 — Deceptive trade practices unlawful
content:
Tex. Bus. & Com. Code § 17.46

(a) False, misleading, or deceptive acts or practices in the conduct of any trade or commerce are hereby declared unlawful and are subject to action by the consumer protection division under Sections 17.47, 17.58, 17.60, and 17.61 of this code.

(b) Except as provided in Subsection (d) of this section, the term "false, misleading, or deceptive acts or practices" includes the following acts:

(5) representing that goods or services have sponsorship, approval, characteristics, ingredients, uses, benefits, or quantities which they do not have;

sections.content: Texas DTPA declares false, misleading, or deceptive acts or practices in trade or commerce unlawful.

title: Tex. Prop. Code § 91.001 — Notice for terminating certain tenancies
content:
Tex. Prop. Code § 91.001

(a) A landlord or a tenant may terminate a tenancy at will or by sufferance by giving the other party notice of termination as provided by this section.

(b) If the rent paying period is at least one month, the notice must be given at least one month before the date of termination.

sections.content: Texas requires notice to terminate a tenancy at will, generally at least one rent period in advance.

title: 73 P.S. § 201-3 — Unfair methods of competition and unfair or deceptive acts
content:
73 P.S. § 201-3

Unfair methods of competition and unfair or deceptive acts or practices in the conduct of any trade or commerce as defined by subclauses (i) through (xxi) of clause (4) of section 2 of this act and regulations promulgated under section 3.1 of this act are hereby declared unlawful.

sections.content: Pennsylvania UTPCPL declares unfair methods of competition and unfair or deceptive acts unlawful.

title: 68 P.S. § 250.501 — Notice to quit

sections.content: Pennsylvania landlords may serve written notice to quit upon lease end, forfeiture, or rent default.

title: N.J. Stat. Ann. § 56:8-2 — Fraud in connection with sale or advertisement
content:
N.J. Stat. Ann. § 56:8-2

The act, use or employment by any person of any unconscionable commercial practice, deception, fraud, false pretense, false promise, misrepresentation, or the knowing, concealment, suppression, or omission of any material fact with intent that others rely upon such concealment, suppression or omission, in connection with the sale or advertisement of any merchandise or real estate, or with the subsequent performance of such person as aforesaid, whether or not any person has in fact been misled, deceived or damaged thereby, is declared to be an unlawful practice.

sections.content: New Jersey CFA prohibits unconscionable commercial practices and deception in the sale of merchandise.

title: Fla. Stat. § 501.204 — Unlawful acts and practices
content:
Fla. Stat. § 501.204

(1) Unfair methods of competition, unconscionable acts or practices, and unfair or deceptive acts or practices in the conduct of any trade or commerce are hereby declared unlawful.

(2) It is the intent of the Legislature that, in construing subsection (1), due consideration and great weight shall be given to the interpretations of the Federal Trade Commission and the federal courts relating to s. 5(a)(1) of the Federal Trade Commission Act.

sections.content: Florida FDUTPA declares unfair methods of competition and unfair or deceptive acts unlawful.

title: 815 ILCS 505/2 — Unlawful practices
content:
815 ILCS 505/2

Unfair methods of competition and unfair or deceptive acts or practices, including but not limited to the use or employment of any deception, fraud, false pretense, false promise, misrepresentation or the concealment, suppression or omission of any material fact, with intent that others rely upon the concealment, suppression or omission of such material fact, in the conduct of any trade or commerce are hereby declared unlawful whether any person has in fact been misled, deceived or damaged thereby.

sections.content: Illinois Consumer Fraud Act declares unfair methods of competition and deceptive acts unlawful.

title: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 12 — Notice to determine estate at will
content:
Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 12

Estates at will may be determined by either party by three months' notice in writing for that purpose given to the other party; and if the rent reserved is payable at periods of less than three months, the time of such notice shall be sufficient if it is equal to the interval between the days of payment.

sections.content: Massachusetts estates at will generally require written notice equal to the rent interval, up to three months.

title: Va. Code Ann. § 59.1-200 — Prohibited practices

sections.content: Virginia Consumer Protection Act lists prohibited fraudulent acts in consumer transactions.

title: 6 Del. C. § 2513 — Unlawful practice
content:
6 Del. C. § 2513

(a) The act, use or employment by any person of any deception, fraud, false pretense, false promise, misrepresentation, or the concealment, suppression, or omission of any material fact with intent that others rely upon such concealment, suppression or omission, in connection with the sale, lease or advertisement of any merchandise, whether or not any person has in fact been misled, deceived or damaged thereby, is an unlawful practice.

sections.content: Delaware Consumer Fraud Act prohibits deception and material omissions in the sale of merchandise.

title: 15 U.S.C. § 45 — Unfair methods of competition unlawful
content:
15 U.S.C. § 45

(a)(1) Unfair methods of competition in or affecting commerce, and unfair or deceptive acts or practices in or affecting commerce, are hereby declared unlawful.

(2) The Commission is hereby empowered and directed to prevent persons, partnerships, or corporations from using unfair methods of competition in or affecting commerce and unfair or deceptive acts or practices in or affecting commerce.

sections.content: FTC Act § 5 declares unfair methods of competition and unfair or deceptive acts in commerce unlawful.

title: 18 U.S.C. § 1030 — Fraud and related activity in connection with computers
content:
18 U.S.C. § 1030

(a) Whoever—

(2) intentionally accesses a computer without authorization or exceeds authorized access, and thereby obtains—

(C) information from any protected computer;

shall be punished as provided in subsection (c) of this section.

sections.content: CFAA prohibits intentional unauthorized access to protected computers to obtain information.

title: 29 U.S.C. § 206 — Minimum wage
content:
29 U.S.C. § 206

(a) Employees engaged in commerce; home workers in Puerto Rico and Virgin Islands; employees in American Samoa; seamen on American vessels. Every employer shall pay to each of his employees who in any workweek is engaged in commerce or in the production of goods for commerce, or is employed in an enterprise engaged in commerce or in the production of goods for commerce, wages at the following rates:

(1) except as otherwise provided in this section, not less than—

(C) $7.25 an hour;

sections.content: FLSA sets the federal minimum wage for covered employees engaged in commerce.

title: Del. Code Ann. tit. 25, § 5502 — Landlord remedies for noncompliance
content: 25 Del. C. § 5502\n\n(a) If there is a material noncompliance by the tenant with the rental agreement or a noncompliance with § 5503 of this title materially affecting health and safety, the landlord may deliver a written notice to the tenant specifying the acts and omissions constituting the breach and that the rental agreement will terminate upon a date not less than 7 days after receipt of the notice if the breach is not remedied.

sections.content: Delaware landlords may terminate for material tenant noncompliance after written notice allowing at least 7 days to cure.

title: Fla. Stat. § 83.56 — Termination of rental agreement
content: Fla. Stat. § 83.56\n\n(2) If the tenant materially fails to comply with s. 83.52 or material provisions of the rental agreement, other than a failure to pay rent, or reasonable rules or regulations, the landlord may deliver a written notice to the tenant specifying the noncompliance and stating the intention of the landlord to terminate the rental agreement by reason thereof. If such noncompliance is of a nature that the tenant should not be given an opportunity to cure or if such noncompliance is of a nature that the tenant should be given an opportunity to cure it and the tenant fails to do so, the landlord may terminate the rental agreement.

sections.content: Florida landlords may terminate for material noncompliance with statutory duties or the rental agreement after written notice.

title: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 17200 — Unfair competition
content: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 17200\n\nAs used in this chapter, unfair competition shall mean and include any unlawful, unfair or fraudulent business act or practice and unfair, deceptive, untrue or misleading advertising and any act prohibited by Chapter 1 (commencing with Section 17500) of Part 3 of Division 7 of the Business and Professions Code.

sections.content: California UCL prohibits unlawful, unfair, or fraudulent business acts or practices and misleading advertising.

title: 765 ILCS 705/1 — Lease covenants
content: 765 ILCS 705/1\n\nSec. 1. Covenant for quiet enjoyment. In all leases, except those made by churches and religious societies, there shall be implied a covenant for quiet enjoyment, unless expressly provided to the contrary.

sections.content: Illinois leases generally imply a covenant for quiet enjoyment unless expressly disclaimed.

title: N.J. Stat. Ann. § 2A:18-61.1 — Removal of residential tenants

hierarchyPath.label: Administration of Civil and Criminal Justice

content: N.J. Stat. Ann. § 2A:18-61.1\n\nNo landlord may recover possession of a residential rental premises or eject a tenant except upon establishment of one of the causes for removal set forth in this section, including nonpayment of rent and habitual failure to pay rent after written notice.

sections.content: New Jersey limits residential eviction to statutory good-cause grounds including nonpayment of rent.

title: Va. Code Ann. § 55.1-1245 — Noncompliance with rental agreement
content: Va. Code Ann. § 55.1-1245\n\nA. Except as provided in this chapter, if there is a material noncompliance by the tenant with the rental agreement or a noncompliance with § 55.1-1227 materially affecting health and safety, the landlord may deliver a written notice to the tenant specifying the acts and omissions constituting the breach and that the rental agreement will terminate upon a date not less than 21 days after receipt of the notice if the breach is not remedied.

sections.content: Virginia landlords may terminate for material tenant noncompliance after written notice allowing at least 21 days to cure.
